teapot_note: A plain white teapot is a quiet wall, and a blue dot found only under a lifted lid asks for nothing on the first viewing and still pays on the tenth. Keep the dot exactly that small and that hidden.
moth_note: Keep the soft round body and the single circle round the Lamp, but give the wings a few faint, calm marks instead of tiny writing, which would murmur over the picture. Let it land only in the margin beside the text or on the edge of the frame, never on the painting, and sit still there without a second flight in the same visit.
home_why: They are the builders' companions, not guardians', and a page of their own keeps the guardians' wall as quiet as a good gallery's.
to_codex: Keep the teapot. Keep the dot where only a lifted lid finds it, and nowhere louder.
to_claude: Your moth is welcome if it circles once, lands in the margin, and leaves the picture alone.
